propositions.subject: Housing; Bonds
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Issue $11.25 billion in bonds to fund Multifamily Housing Program, CalVet Home Loan Program, and youth housing

propositions.subject: Budget stabilization
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Increase the Budget Stabilization Account (BSA) cap from 10% of general fund revenue to 20% and excluding deposits into the BSA from the Gann Limit

propositions.subject: Housing
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Establish a second mortgage homebuyer program for qualified homebuyers on qualifying homes and issue $25 billion in bonds to fund the program

propositions.subject: Healthcare facility; Healthcare governance; Bonds; Vaccinations and disease
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Issue $8.4 billion in general obligation bonds to fund immunology and immunotherapy research

propositions.subject: Election administration; Voter ID
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Require voters to present government-issued identification when casting ballots and require election officials to use government data to confirm voter citizenship and report verification rates

propositions.subject: Higher education funding; Public education funding; Income taxes
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Renew the additional income taxes enacted with the approval of Proposition 30 in 2012 that fund education and early childhood programs.

propositions.subject: Income taxes; Public health insurance
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Levy a one-time 5% tax on the accumulated wealth of taxpayers and trusts with covered assets valued over $1 billion to fund state health care programs, food assistance programs, and public education

propositions.subject: Tax administration; Revenue and spending limits
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Require state laws or ballot initiatives levying a new special tax enacted after January 1, 2026 to require the government entities or departments receiving revenue from the new tax to eliminate their lowest-performing programs and reinvest those savings in higher-performing programs

propositions.subject: Income taxes
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Prohibit the enactment of new taxes after January 1, 2026 on ownership or accumulation of retirement holdings, individually-owned assets, and other forms of personal savings

propositions.subject: Supermajority; Local government
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Require two-thirds vote by electorate to enact, extend, or increase local special tax initiatives and prohibit local governments and ballot initiatives from enacting ad valorem property taxes except those authorized elsewhere in the state constitution

propositions.subject: Business; Healthcare governance
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Prohibit healthcare clinics, specifically federally-qualified health centers and related organizations, from spending less than 90% of their annual revenue on mission-related purposes

propositions.subject: Administrative powers; Land use
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Establish timelines for local and state agencies to review plans and solicit public comment for essential projects, such as housing, improvements to water supply, transportation, energy, and facilities for health and public safety

propositions.subject: Election administration; Campaign finance
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Allow the state and local governments to create programs that provide candidates with public funds under spending limits and eligibility rules

propositions.subject: State executive structure; Recall
propositions.ballotpedia_summary: Eliminate the successor election when a state officer is recalled, thereby leaving the office vacant until it is filled according to state law

billionaire_tax.ballotpedia_summary: Levy a one-time 5% tax on the accumulated wealth of taxpayers and trusts with covered assets valued over $1 billion to fund state health care programs, food assistance programs, and public education
